_note: Marisol Castellanos golden fixture — the first successful paid_47 Full Diagnostic generation (2026-10-28, contact DeubTUGSn9U9IL4layqU). This fixture captures the agent response shape the paid47-v2 contract targets: three primary gaps anchored to the AR aging + growth supportability + pricing diagnostic (NOT merchant processing, which was previously surfacing as a primary gap on nothing but an opportunity flag). The structural tests in paid47_v2_golden.test.js read this file, so a regression that shifts the primary diagnoses back onto a flag-only basis fails those tests.
headline: Growth is outrunning your cash and visibility discipline.
opener: Marisol, you're running a growing business on a thinner cash cushion than it looks. Your A/R aging is drifting older, you're pricing without a formal cost build-up, and most decisions are coming from the bank balance instead of a close.
context: Three issues, one financial conversation: the cash you've already earned isn't landing fast enough, your pricing may be leaving margin on the table, and you can't tell either way without a monthly close.

financialSnapshot.label: A/R 60+ days
financialSnapshot.meaning: 32.1% of overdue A/R is already in 60+.

financialSnapshot.label: 60+ A/R as months of debt service

gaps.title: A/R aging is drifting older, not holding steady
gaps.known: $9,000 of your $28,000 overdue A/R is already 60+ days — about a third of the overdue bucket.
gaps.diagnosis: Collections are not keeping up with aging; the problem is drifting older, not holding at 30+. At $850/mo in debt service, that 60+ bucket represents 10.6 months of obligations tied up as receivables.
gaps.whyItMatters: Cash you've already earned is sitting with customers instead of covering debt and payroll.
gaps.unknown: Which customers hold the 60+ balance and whether any are at genuine collection risk.
gaps.decisionImplication: Running a 30/60/90 collections sweep before adding another hire will unlock cash you already own.

gaps.title: Growth is outpacing financial visibility
gaps.known: You said decisions are made from bank balance, and you don't have a documented budget.
gaps.diagnosis: You can see cash in but you can't see cost drift, so scaling adds risk you can't quantify.
gaps.whyItMatters: The next hire or next piece of equipment lands on top of a cost base you aren't tracking monthly.
gaps.unknown: What your actual monthly close cadence is and whether any management reporting exists.
gaps.decisionImplication: Stand up a monthly close before the next headcount decision.

gaps.title: Pricing is not anchored to a cost build-up
gaps.known: Pricing was set without a formal cost build-up and hasn't been reviewed against current costs.
gaps.diagnosis: Each new job carries unknown margin — some may be unprofitable at today's cost base.
gaps.whyItMatters: Volume growth on thin or negative margin makes the cash problem worse, not better.
gaps.unknown: True gross margin by service line.
gaps.decisionImplication: Rebuild one or two highest-volume prices from cost up before adding volume.

opportunities.title: Tighten the collections cycle
opportunities.whyCredible: $9,000 of overdue A/R is already past 60 days — a measured problem, not a hunch.
opportunities.whatMustBeTrue: You have the staff capacity to run structured 30/60/90 outreach.
opportunities.nextValidation: One week of logged outreach + outcome counts.

opportunities.title: Rebuild pricing from cost up on top-volume lines
opportunities.whyCredible: You said pricing has not been reviewed against cost; that gap is a direct margin lever.
opportunities.whatMustBeTrue: You can isolate a top-two service line that drives most of the revenue.
opportunities.nextValidation: One cost build-up compared to current price for that line.

connections.title: Collections drag + pricing drift + weak visibility are one problem
connections.explanation: You're growing on cash you haven't collected, at prices you haven't verified, without a monthly close that would surface either issue in time to course-correct.

questionsToClarify.question: Which customers hold the 60+ A/R balance and are any at genuine collection risk?
questionsToClarify.whyItMatters: Changes whether the fix is outreach cadence or write-down policy.

questionsToClarify.question: What is your actual monthly close cadence today?
questionsToClarify.whyItMatters: Decides whether the first move is a close or a full financial-visibility rebuild.

questionsToClarify.question: What are your top two service lines by revenue?
questionsToClarify.whyItMatters: Scopes the cost-based pricing rebuild to a tractable surface area.

decisionOrder.action: Run a 30/60/90 A/R collections sweep this week.
decisionOrder.whyNow: You already earned this cash; nothing is faster than collecting it.
Everything downstream depends on seeing the P&L monthly.

decisionOrder.action: Rebuild pricing on top-two service lines from cost up.

nextStepBody: Miguel will walk through these three findings, press on the two open questions above, and help you pick the first move. The strategist review is included with the Full Diagnostic — book the time that works.
strategistBrief: Marisol scored needs-attention. Three primary gaps anchored to A/R aging (deterministic ratio), growth-visibility (bank-balance decision basis + no budget), and pricing-cost alignment. Merchant processing is a flag but not a primary diagnostic — do NOT lead the call there. Top probe: what the actual close cadence is, which 60+ customers are at risk, and the top-two service lines by revenue.
